correctness.rationale: PASS. For p>=q>=3, deleting two edges leaves connected K_pq; Laplacian eigenspaces for the two parts and their contrast yield explicit r,k,c,d. Rank-two Woodbury inversion on the constant-orthogonal subspace gives Delta=2(p+q)[k(1-r)+cd]/[(1-r)^2-c²], and all denominators are strictly positive. Substitution for the three edge motifs gives positive pairwise interactions, Delta_A>Delta_D, Delta_A-Delta_B proportional to p-q, and Delta_B-Delta_D opposite in sign to cubic H_q(p). Descartes plus H_q(q)<0, H_q(T-1)<0, H_q(T)>0 with T=q(q-1)^2 establishes the sole p>=q crossover strictly inside (T-1,T), hence integer threshold with no tie. Independently checked all symbolic difference and bracket identities and 54 rational finite sign comparisons, including q=3 and boundary T-1,T; finite tests are not a substitute for the all-p,q proof.

originality.rationale: PASS, best-of-knowledge. Ge and Dong explicitly evaluate effective resistances and Kirchhoff index for deletion of an arbitrary matching from K_mn, covering the D motif (which is credited), but not incident two-edge motifs or their sharp ranking with D. Yang gives general bipartite Kirchhoff extrema without this fixed-part-size deletion comparison. Jiang–He–Liu–Li give diameter-three bipartite extrema; only title/abstract were available, and its complete text remains an access risk, so no unsupported whole-document noncoverage claim is made. The finite sharp cubic crossing is additional to generic spectral rank-two update tools.
residual_risks: Full text of Jiang–He–Liu–Li 2020 was not accessible; the authorized source returned vpn_disconnected. Any specific prior pairwise assertion inside it remains uninspected; the abstract, however, addresses diameter-constrained global extremes.
